Jeremiah 1:1

The word of God that came upon Jeremiah son of Hilkiah, one of the priests, who lived in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin,

  1. Jeremiah 11:21-23 historical connection through Anathoth

    Jeremiah is introduced as a priest living in Anathoth. The later passage names men of Anathoth who demand that the prophet stop speaking in the Lord's name, connecting his hometown with opposition to his commission.

    Read matching passage

    Jeremiah 11:21 Therefore thus says the Lord concerning the men of Anathoth who seek my soul, who say: You must certainly not prophesy in the Lord’s name; otherwise you will die by our hands.

    Jeremiah 11:22 Behold, I will visit them; their young men will die by the sword, and their sons and daughters will end their lives in famine,

    Jeremiah 11:23 and no remnant of them will remain, because I will bring evils upon those dwelling in Anathoth in the year of their visitation.

    Pinned source record

Jeremiah 1:2

which became God’s word to him in the days of Josiah son of Amos, king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his reign.

  1. 2 Chronicles 34:3 regnal chronology of Josiah's reforms and Jeremiah's calling

    Jeremiah dates the beginning of God's word to Josiah's thirteenth year. Chronicles dates Josiah's beginning to cleanse Judah and Jerusalem to his twelfth year, providing adjacent regnal chronology without identifying the calling and the purge as the same event.

    Read matching passage

    2 Chronicles 34:3 In the eighth year of his reign, while still a boy, he began to seek the Lord, the God of his father David. In the twelfth year of his reign he began to cleanse Judah and Jerusalem of the high places, sacred groves, and cast objects.

Jeremiah 1:3

It also came in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, until the eleventh year of Zedekiah son of Josiah, king of Judah, until Jerusalem’s captivity in the fifth month.

  1. 2 Kings 25:2-11 historical counterpart to Jerusalem's captivity

    Jeremiah's heading ends with Zedekiah's eleventh year and Jerusalem's captivity in the fifth month. Kings records the siege lasting to Sedekias's eleventh year and the fifth-month destruction and removal of Jerusalem's population; the royal name forms differ.

    Read matching passage

    2 Kings 25:2 The city remained under siege until King Sedekias’s eleventh year.

    2 Kings 25:3 On the ninth of the month the famine grew severe in the city, and there were no loaves for the people of the land.

    2 Kings 25:4 The city was breached, and all the men of war went out by night by way of the gate between the walls, the one belonging to the king’s garden, with the Chaldeans surrounding the city. He went by the way of the Araba.

    2 Kings 25:5 The Chaldean force pursued the king and overtook him in Araboth Jericho, and all his force scattered away from him.

    2 Kings 25:6 They seized the king and brought him to the king of Babylon at Deblatha, and he pronounced judgment upon him.

    2 Kings 25:7 He slaughtered Sedekias’s sons before his eyes. He blinded Sedekias’s eyes, bound him with fetters, and brought him to Babylon.

    2 Kings 25:8 In the fifth month, on the seventh of the month, in the nineteenth year of Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon, Nabouzardan, the chief cook who stood before the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.

    2 Kings 25:9 He set fire to the Lord’s house, the king’s house, and all Jerusalem’s houses; every house was set ablaze by

    2 Kings 25:10 the chief cook.

    2 Kings 25:11 Nabouzardan, the chief cook, removed the rest of the people left in the city, those who had gone over to the king of Babylon, and the remaining support.

    Exodus 4:11 The Lord said to Moses, “Who gave a human being a mouth? Who made one hard of hearing or deaf, seeing or blind? Is it not I, God?

    Exodus 4:12 Now therefore go, and I will open your mouth, and teach you what you are to speak.”
